question.:question/problem: Given  $f(x,y)=4\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y$, find $∇f(x,y).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y) \\  & =4y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y) \\  & =4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{y} \\  & =4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+\frac{{x}^{2}}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\text{ }j \\  & =(4y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡y)\text{ }i+(4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+\frac{{x}^{2}}{y})\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Hence, the gradient is:

$$
